name: Can a faulty water heater cause low water pressure?

mainEntity.name: Can a faulty water heater cause low water pressure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, a faulty water heater can contribute to low water pressure, particularly if sediment buildup inside the tank restricts water flow or if there's a problem with the heater's shut-off valve. When hot water lines are affected, but cold water lines are not, a water heater issue is a strong possibility. We often check water heaters during pressure diagnostics. Recognizing this as a potential cause can guide initial troubleshooting and help you describe the symptoms more accurately to a plumber, allowing for quicker and more targeted diagnosis.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, a faulty water heater can cause low water pressure due to sediment buildup or valve issues, especially if only hot water lines are affected. This helps guide diagnosis.
